The change adds `App/Sources/Features/RemoteMirror/Conversation/` (conversation event model, Claude Code and Codex transcript adapters, bounded log, transcript tail, status mapper, feed) and tests under `App/Tests/RemoteMirror/` (`MirrorConversation*Tests.swift`, `ClaudeConversationAdapterTests.swift`, `CodexConversationAdapterTests.swift`, `MirrorTranscriptTailTests.swift`). Rules for this review:
- Read-only. Do not run `xcodebuild`, `make`, `swift build`, `swift test` or any test: another reviewer is running tests in this checkout and a second build would hang both.
- No git writes, no branch switches, no file edits.
- Focus on `CodexConversationAdapter.swift`: compare it with real Codex rollouts under `~/.codex/sessions/` (the newest files are 0.166.0) and your own current rollout, and check every field name it reads (`item_completed`, `task_started`, `task_complete`, `turn_aborted`, `turn_context`, `thread_settings_applied`, item types `CommandExecution`, `FileChange`, `McpToolCall`, `Extension`, `ImageView`, `UserMessage`, `AgentMessage`, `Reasoning`, `ContextCompaction`). Then review the rest for correctness.
- Every finding needs a `path:line` reference and a severity (P1 wrong behaviour, P2 edge case, P3 style). Mark anything you could not verify as unverified. End with a short summary listing verified claims and open questions.


---
Prowl dispatch completion protocol v1:
Before ending this task, choose exactly one terminal outcome and make this command your final tool action:
prowl agents dispatch-complete --outcome succeeded|failed --summary "<concise result>"
Use succeeded only when the assigned work is complete and verified. Use failed when it cannot be completed.
Keep the required summary to a single line with no control characters, and explain the result clearly.
Do not omit the command; Prowl supplies its dispatch context
automatically.

| | |

| **Status** | Planned |

| **Primary PRs** | (fill in as they merge) |

## Background

Mobile mirrors render `text-v1`: the Host's terminal viewport as plain text, reflowed on
the phone. For an agent TUI (Claude Code, Codex) this is a rendering of a conversation
made for an 80-column terminal: box-drawing composer borders, a status footer, spinner
frames and hard-wrapped tool output. On an iPhone it is unusable (device check on
2026-11-03: the composer box became a column of horizontal rules, the footer took the
bottom third of the screen, the transcript was lost in between).

Decision with onevcat (2026-11-04): the Host normalizes agent events into a Prowl-defined
conversation event set and streams those; the phone renders a chat-style GUI; the user can
switch to the plain-text Screen view to see the real Host state; panes without an agent or
with an unsupported agent fall back to `text-v1`. This entry records the capability
boundary found by the spike and the plan built on it.

## Goals

- A `conversation-v1` representation beside `vt-v1` / `text-v1`, additive on the wire.
- One event model for every supported agent; per-agent adapters on the Host only.
- Prompts that need a person (permission, question, auth) are events with the content
  the Host can prove, and can be answered from the phone without replaying input.
- Session changes (`/clear`, `/new`, resume, fork) are explicit events; an uncertain
  mapping sends the client to the Screen view instead of showing stale content.
- Reconnect resumes from the last seen sequence; a bounded snapshot replaces history paging.

### Non-goals

- Token-level streaming of assistant text (no source provides it; see Boundaries).
- Replacing the terminal: Screen view, Mac `vt-v1`, History and remote scrolling stay.
- Push notifications and an internet relay (issue #989 items 1–2); the event model only
  carries what a later notification needs (pane, kind, one-line summary).
- Agents beyond Claude Code and Codex in the first release.

# Prowl dispatch completion

## When to use

Use when a Prowl task explicitly requires `prowl agents dispatch-complete` as the final tool action, an exact completion summary, or a receipt after completion. Do not use for ordinary Prowl development that has no dispatch protocol.

## Inputs / context

1. Read the task for its required outcome, exact summary text, required receipt, and constraints such as no edits or no Git.
2. Confirm the intended working directory if the task requires it. If the task supplies a `PROWL_CLI_SOCKET` and repository-local Debug CLI, record that exact pair; it overrides the normal installed CLI only for this invocation.
3. If the task constrains terminal command count or says “that same background terminal,” retain each returned session ID and do not start a replacement process.
4. Identify all verification that must happen before completion.

## Procedure

1. Perform only the authorized work. For narrowly scoped file edits, limit edits and checks to the stated target; do not run Git when forbidden.
2. Run the needed verification and retain concrete evidence. For file creation, check each requested path with `test -f`; a listing may show pre-existing siblings. For a background terminal, wait on its returned session until an exit result is observed. For independently requested concurrent terminals, start and poll the returned sessions together.
3. Decide the outcome honestly: use `succeeded` only when all required work is complete and verified; otherwise use the required failed outcome or stop for direction.
4. Construct a concise, single-line summary. Preserve user-supplied exact wording verbatim.
5. As the final tool action, run the exact user-supplied completion command. If no executable/socket is supplied, run:

   `prowl agents dispatch-complete --outcome <succeeded|failed> --summary "<summary>"`

6. After the command reports its terminal result, provide any exact user-required receipt. Do not make another tool call.

## Efficiency plan

- Gather all checks before step 5; the final-action invariant rules out post-completion diagnostics.
- For exact terminal probes, reuse the initial session(s); poll concurrent sessions in one parallel call to reduce elapsed time without changing command cardinality.
- When a probe mandates a socket/Debug binary, do not test a second endpoint: use the supplied pair once after verification.
- Prefer direct target-path checks over repository-wide exploration for constrained file tasks.
- Stop before step 5 if required verification is missing; do not manufacture a success outcome.
